description: Variation of condition 1 (approved drawings) attached to planning permission ref 2024/2793 dated 19/12/2025 for the conversion of the ground floor flat into 2 self-contained dwellings comprising 2 x 2 bed 4 person dwellings alongside the excavation of the basement, erection of single storey side rear extension and associated elevational alterations including the installation of two side entrance doors to Henry Road, a bike store and a front lightwell. The variation seeks to increase the basement excavation alongside alterations to the ground floor extension and rooflights, elevational changes and internal reconfiguration.
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed enlargement of the basement extension and its continuous mini-piled retaining perimeter would permanently encroach into the Root Protection Area (RPA) of an adjacent off-site Silver Birch street tree (T1) on Henry Road. In the absence of empirical trial pit data demonstrating otherwise, the excavation and permanent loss of rooting soil volume would sever roots and likely result in the irreversible decline and eventual loss of a prominent street tree of high public amenity and ecological value. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy LP51 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (LP33), Policy G7 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy N3 the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).</p>

<p>The proposed replacement boundary treatment along the Henry Road elevation falls outside the scope of the operative description of development granted under original planning permission ref. 2024/2793 (dated 19/12/2025), and requires planning permission in its own right by virtue of its height exceeding 1 metre adjacent to a highway. Consequently, the proposed works cannot lawfully be permitted by way of a variation of condition under Section 73 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).</p>

<p>The proposed enlargement of the basement extension, by virtue of its excessive footprint exceeding 1.5 times the original host building footprint, its encroachment beyond 50% of the depth of both the original building and the rear garden, and its failure to provide a minimum 1-metre depth of suitable soil cover above the extended subterranean structure, represents an overdevelopment of the site that fails to provide an optimum arrangement in terms of form, mass, and scale or safeguard local biodiversity and natural drainage capacity. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D1, D3, and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy LP1 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (LP33), and the adopted Hackney Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2025).</p>

<p>In the absence of a completed Deed of Variation (or supplemental legal agreement) pursuant to Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) to carry forward the planning obligations attached to planning permission ref. 2024/2793, the proposed development fails to secure a financial contribution towards affordable housing, a carbon offsetting contribution, a car-free restriction preventing future occupiers from applying for on-street parking permits. Consequently, the development would fail to contribute adequately towards local affordable housing need, achieve required reductions in carbon dioxide emissions, or prevent adverse impacts on on-street parking stress, highway safety, and sustainable transport, contrary to Policies H4 (Delivering affordable housing), H5 (Threshold approach to applications), SI2 (Minimising greenhouse gas emissions), T1 (Strategic approach to transport), and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021), Policies LP12 (Housing Supply), LP13 (Affordable Housing), LP43 (Transport and Land Use), LP45 (Parking), LP54 (Overheating and Adapting to Climate Change), and LP55 (Mitigating Climate Change) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (LP33), the Hackney Planning Contributions Supplementary Planning Document (2020), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).</p>
